Ammo spread while aiming
tooltip: The same thing while aiming down sights (vanilla 1.0, two rounds sit at 10.0 - those are the ones that are meant to be fired from the hip). Not play-tested yet.

label: Ammo bleeding
tooltip: How much bleeding a hit from this round causes. Vanilla is 1.0 on every round, so this is a clean global dial; 0 % = rounds never start bleeding. The weapon's own bleeding value applies on top. Not play-tested yet.

label: Ammo cover penetration
tooltip: How well bullets punch through wooden walls, fences etc.

label: Ammo spread
tooltip: Spread the round itself adds (vanilla 1.0 on 33 of the 35 rounds, 1.2 on two). 0 % = the round adds no spread at all. Stacks with the weapon spread slider. Not play-tested yet.

label: Ammo trajectory flatness
tooltip: Higher = flatter flight path, so less drop at distance. Vanilla runs from 1.0 to 1.9 depending on the round, and this scales each one. Not play-tested yet.

label: Ammo pack size
tooltip: How many rounds one picked-up pack contains (vanilla 30 for rifle rounds, 10 to 50 for the rest). Launcher grenades come one at a time in vanilla and stay that way. Whole numbers, never below one. Not play-tested yet.

label: Ammo recoil
tooltip: Recoil contributed by the round itself (vanilla 1.0 everywhere). Stacks with the weapon recoil slider and with recoil upgrades. Not play-tested yet.

label: Ammo stack size
tooltip: How many rounds fit in one inventory slot (vanilla 900 for every round). × 10 = 9000. Per round in the tree below as the fifth factor. Worth pairing with 'Max carry weight' and 'Item weight': in vanilla you hit the weight limit long before the stack limit - 900 rounds of 7.62 already weigh 21.6 kg of your 80. Not play-tested yet.

label: Ammo weapon wear
tooltip: How hard a round is on the barrel (vanilla 0.8 to 1.3 - cheap rounds wear more). 0 % = this round never wears the weapon. Stacks with the weapon durability slider. Not play-tested yet.

Body armor prevents limping (experimental)
tooltip: Enables each body armor's native anti-limp flag. Per-armor explicit values take priority. Separate from knockdown immunity. Not play-tested.

label: Remove armor sprint restrictions (experimental)
tooltip: Removes only the armor effect that blocks sprinting. Sprint speed is unchanged. Per-armor explicit Off keeps that armor's original restriction. Not play-tested.

label: Anomaly wear on gear
tooltip: How much condition an anomaly hit costs your armour, helmet and both weapons (vanilla 0.2 to 25 per hit depending on the anomaly - the Clicker and Carousel are the brutal ones). 0 % = anomalies no longer damage your gear at all. Separate from the butt-strike slider in the Weapons tab. Not play-tested yet.

label: Armor carry-weight bonuses
tooltip: Exoskeleton & armor/upgrade carry bonuses. 0 % = armor grants no extra carry weight.

label: Armor wear coefficient (experimental)
tooltip: The game's ArmorDurabilityParamsCoef and HelmetDurabilityParamsCoef (vanilla 0.7). They tie a piece's condition to its protection, but the direction is unknown: either 'protection left at zero durability' or the opposite. Try 0.3 against 1.0 in-game and tell us. Not play-tested yet.

label: Extra artifact slots on every body armor
tooltip: Adds slots to each body armor's own count (vanilla: most have 2, a few 0, 1, 3 or 4, three have 5). Capped at 5, the game's maximum. Helmets are untouched. Like the 'Armor Artifact Slots' mod. Not play-tested yet.

label: Stamina & bleeding caps
tooltip: The same list holds two more ceilings that nothing else here touches: stamina regeneration from artifacts and upgrades stops counting at 30, bleeding resistance at 5. Worth raising if you stack stamina artifacts. Not play-tested yet.

label: Armor durability
tooltip: Armor takes more punishment before breaking.

label: Weapon & armor max condition
tooltip: The condition bar's full length - vanilla runs from 1,125 to 3,000 for guns and 520 to 1,040 for armor. 500 % = five times as much to wear through, like 'Better Durability'. ⚠ An item's condition is stored in your save, so this only shows on gear that spawns AFTER you install the mod. Not play-tested yet.

label: Armor grenade resistance
tooltip: How much grenade and explosion damage each armor class absorbs (vanilla 0 / 10 / 20 / 40 / 60 % for physical protection classes 0-4, capped at 100 %). 0 % = grenades ignore armor. Not play-tested yet.

label: Protection caps
tooltip: The game caps your total protection at 90 % (85 % radiation, physical 4.5) - anything armor and artifacts give beyond that is lost. 111 % lifts the percent caps to 100 (the maximum), physical scales freely. Like the 'Max Stats Patch'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Base guards use normal weapon damage (no instant death)
tooltip: Vanilla guard weapons deal 500 damage per hit and restricted areas kill you with an invisible sniper shot; this gives guards their weapon's normal NPC damage and removes the sniper effect (like 'NoInstaGibByGuards'). Guards are meant to be deadly - use at your own risk. Not play-tested yet.

label: Hit camera shake (aim punch)
tooltip: Camera kick when YOU get shot. 0 % = no flinch, 300 % = heavy aim punch. Confirmed at 300 % by craigduk76 (GitHub #14).

label: Armor vs. anomaly strike weight (experimental)
tooltip: How strongly your armor rating counts against the physical strike of anomalies (vanilla coefficient 1.0, the sibling of the bullet weight above; formula unknown). Not play-tested yet.

label: Armor vs. bullet difference weight
tooltip: How strongly the gap between armor rating and bullet penetration changes damage (vanilla coefficients 2.0 global, 1.6 projectiles, 1.3 melee). Experimental, not play-tested.

label: Damage to unaware NPCs
tooltip: Your hits on NPCs that have not noticed you deal 2.5x in vanilla (a hidden sneak-attack bonus). Not play-tested yet.

label: Armor deflection chance
tooltip: Chance that armor far above a bullet's class deflects the hit (vanilla 93 %). Experimental, not play-tested.

label: Deflected-hit damage
tooltip: Damage coefficient of a deflected hit on humans and mutants (vanilla 1.5). Experimental, not play-tested.

label: Weapon durability
tooltip: Weapons wear less per shot fired.

label: Explosion armor damage
tooltip: How much an explosion wears your armor and NPC armor (vanilla 20 to 50 per blast). 0 % = blasts hurt but leave the suit intact. Not play-tested yet.

label: Explosion armor penetration
tooltip: How well a blast goes through armor (vanilla 4 to 6). Lower = heavy armor protects more against grenades. Not play-tested yet.

label: Explosion damage to objects
tooltip: Damage to destructible props - crates, barrels, gas bottles (vanilla 1000 to 4000). Not play-tested yet.

label: Explosion damage to NPCs
tooltip: The DamageNPC value of every explosion type (vanilla RGD-5 260, RPG 2700). Damage to YOU is the slider above. Not play-tested yet.

label: Explosion radius
tooltip: Blast, impulse and concussion radius of grenades, launcher rounds, barrels and gas cylinders (vanilla RGD-5 7 m, F1 10 m). Like 'IncreaseGrenadeRadius'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Weapon jamming
tooltip: × 0 = weapons never jam.

label: Last-bullet damage multiplier
tooltip: A hidden multiplier the game keeps for the last bullet (vanilla 2.0). Honest note: which shot it applies to is not verified - x 1 switches it off. Not play-tested yet.

label: Player damage (guns)
tooltip: Applied via difficulty multipliers, all difficulty levels.

label: Ragdoll force on death
tooltip: How hard a body is thrown by the shot that kills it (vanilla multipliers 2 and 3 on every prototype). 0 % = bodies drop where they stand. Cosmetic. Not play-tested yet.

label: Reputation doesn't affect repair prices
tooltip: Vanilla charges by standing: enemies pay double, disaffected 1.5x, neutral normal, friends 25 % less. This puts every level on the neutral price. Not play-tested yet.

label: Accept several jobs from one giver (experimental repair)
tooltip: Take a job, then interact with the giver again to take another; the conversation does not open automatically. Each job now has its own journal entry. The round only ends when no accepted job is active. The shared cancel line cancels all current jobs from that giver. Molkerr reports separate hand-ins and save/load working in 1.39. 1.40 still showed missing texts and lost completed-job markers. This experimental revision reapplies markers for remaining ready-to-return jobs and extends the original translation files for ALL installed languages. Both changes need a game test. The larger pak conflicts with mods replacing those same translation files. Use a save from before accepting jobs; old active jobs cannot be migrated. Keep the same pak until all jobs are finished or cancelled. Journal state is saved by the game.

label: Trader buy prices (what you get)
tooltip: Since 1.28.0 this also patches the nine traders that carry their own buy coefficient on the NPC itself (precedence between the two is unverified).

label: Device prices (binoculars, night vision)
tooltip: The two remaining per-category price factors. Not play-tested yet.

label: Fast travel cost
tooltip: 0 % = guides take you anywhere for free.

label: NPC rumour refresh
tooltip: Game hours before stalkers have something new to say (vanilla 24). Lower = fresh rumours and hints sooner. Not play-tested yet.

label: Minimum resale value
tooltip: Broken gear never sells for less than this share of its price (vanilla 10 %). Not play-tested yet.

label: Weapon prices
tooltip: Per-category price multipliers – these stack with the trader buy/sell sliders above.

label: Repair cost
tooltip: 0 % = free repairs.

label: Repeatable quest cooldown
tooltip: Wait time until task givers offer new repeatable jobs (vanilla 24 in-game hours). 0 % = new jobs right away. A cooldown already ticking in your save finishes at its old pace first.

label: Repeatable jobs per round
tooltip: How many jobs a task giver puts on the menu each round (vanilla 3). Each giver is capped at the number of different jobs he actually has (6 to 10). Confirmed in-game by Molkerr on 1.35.0 (GitHub #9): the menu really grows. On its own this is a bigger CHOICE, not more jobs: vanilla lets you take one, and handing it in (or cancelling it) ends the round and starts the cooldown above. To actually take several, use the switch below.

label: Trader sell prices (what you pay)
tooltip: Since 1.28.0 this also patches the nine traders that carry their own sell coefficient on the NPC itself (precedence between the two is unverified).

label: Repair surcharge per upgrade
tooltip: Every part you have fitted makes repairs dearer. Vanilla charges 0.2 per upgrade on top - which is why a fully modded rifle costs a fortune to fix. 0 = upgrades are free to maintain, your repair bill only follows the weapon itself. Same value on all 1288 upgrades in vanilla. Not play-tested yet.

label: Apply the relations above to a running save (experimental)
tooltip: Without this, the values above are the baseline the game reads when a NEW game starts - an existing save keeps its own relations. Switch this on and the mod also ships a tiny quest that sets them on every game launch, using the game's own ChangeRelationships node type (1875 of them in the base game) and its own Scripts/OnGameLaunch folder. This is how 'Relation System Overhaul' (Nexus 2009) does it. Your standing with a faction is the field-proven half; faction-versus-faction rows use the same node but no released mod does that, so treat them as experimental. Not play-tested yet. Remove the pak and the script stops running - relations stay wherever they were last set.

label: Reputation reaction strength
tooltip: How hard kills, heals and assaults move reputation - scales both the local squad reaction and the permanent faction-wide part. 400 % = every action matters four times as much; 25 % = an almost indifferent Zone.

label: Reputation rollback time
tooltip: How long the game remembers LOCAL hostility before forgiving it (vanilla 60 min in the field, faster in hubs). 400 % = grudges last four times longer; 25 % = quick forgiveness. Permanent faction-wide reputation is a separate system and is not affected.

label: Trading requires standing
tooltip: Vanilla: traders deal with you from 'Disaffected' (wary) upward. 'Neutral' or 'Friend' = hardcore reputation play; 'Enemy' = everyone trades with anyone.

label: All mutants trigger anomalies
tooltip: Bloodsuckers, chimeras, controllers, poltergeists, pseudodogs, pseudogiants, deer and rats are immune to anomalies in vanilla; dogs, boars, fleshes, snorks and burers are not. Like 'AnomaliesHitAllMutants'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Mutant harvest: open the loot window instead of the quick animation (experimental)
tooltip: Vanilla harvests mutants with an animation and no loot window (UseMutantLootWithoutWidget = true; both animation sets ship with the game). This flips the flag to false, the loot-window flow. Read from the key name only. Not play-tested yet.

label: Mutants cannot smell you
tooltip: Switches the same scent sensors off (IsActive = false); hearing and sight stay. Not play-tested yet.

label: Bloodsucker cloaking speed
tooltip: × 4 = bloodsuckers vanish almost instantly.

label: Bloodsucker uncloak from damage
tooltip: Higher = hitting them breaks the cloak much harder. × 0 = damage never reveals them.

label: Burer weapon fire interval
tooltip: Seconds between shots of a weapon a burer levitates and fires (vanilla 0.5 to 4 s depending on the ammo type). 200 % = half as many shots. Not play-tested yet.

label: Mutant damage (all species)
tooltip: Via difficulty multiplier – species overrides below scale the individual attack values on top.

label: Mutant hearing range
tooltip: All mutant species share one hearing sensor. Mutants have no config-side vision range – sight is engine logic, so no slider is offered.

label: Mutant physical protection
tooltip: The Protection values of every mutant (vanilla: mostly melee 'Strike' protection, 1 to 4; bullet protection is 0 everywhere and stays 0). × 0 = no protection, like 'No More Tanky Mutants'. Per-species overrides in the tree below. Not play-tested yet.

label: Mutant speed (all species)
tooltip: Walk/run/sprint speed of every mutant species.

label: Mutant attack cooldown
tooltip: Difficulty multiplier on the pause between mutant attacks (vanilla 1.0 on every difficulty). 200 % = mutants attack half as often. Not play-tested yet.

label: Mutant bleeding buildup
tooltip: How fast a mutant hit builds up bleeding. × 0 = claws no longer make you bleed. Bosses and human melee keep their vanilla values. Not play-tested yet.

label: Mutant trophy drop chance
tooltip: Chance that a dead mutant leaves a body part (vanilla: blind dog 15 %, tushkan 10 %, boar/flesh/snork 20 %, bloodsucker 50 %, poltergeist 65 %, the rest 100 %). Capped at 100 %; 1000 % = every mutant drops, like '100% Chance Mutant Loot'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Mutant health regen
tooltip: Mutants passively regenerate health, just like human NPCs (vanilla varies by species). × 0 = wounds stay – the mutant counterpart of 'NPCs don't self-heal'.

label: Mutant attacks per series
tooltip: How many blows a mutant lands in one go before it backs off (vanilla 1 to 3, depending on the attack; many attacks have no series at all and stay that way). Rounded to whole hits, never below one. Human and boss attacks are left alone. Not play-tested yet.

label: Mutant sense of smell
tooltip: Range and speed of the mutants' scent sense. One sensor serves 38 species incl. blind dogs (40 m); chimeras (70 m), fleshes (20 m) and poltergeists (10 m) have their own, front-facing ranges scale along where they exist. Proof it matters: the Weird Flower artifact changes this sense by 60 %. The bad-weather stealth factor (FlairCoef) still applies on top; story bosses are untouched. Not play-tested yet.

label: Pseudodog phantom damage
tooltip: Bite and bleeding of the pseudodog's illusions (vanilla 5 + bleeding). 0 % = phantoms are harmless, like 'NoPseudoDogCloneDamage'. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPCs don't self-heal
tooltip: Vanilla: NPCs passively regenerate health (guards up to 20 HP/s) while the player regenerates none. Includes bosses.

label: NPCs don't loot bodies
tooltip: Human NPCs stop searching corpses (vanilla: they take gear before you arrive). Like 'NPCsDontLootCorpses'. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPCs don't pick up weapons
tooltip: Vanilla NPCs grab weapons from bodies and the ground (better ones by price). Not play-tested yet.

label: Psy fields spawn phantoms instead of real stalkers
tooltip: The psy-field effect normally spawns real hostile NPCs; this switches it to the harmless phantom variant (like 'NoPsyStalkerSpawns'). Not play-tested yet.

label: Max simultaneous NPCs & mutants
tooltip: Vanilla: 52 A-Life agents around the player. 200 % = a much busier Zone (heavy CPU load!).

label: A-Life spawn distance
tooltip: Vanilla: squads spawn ≥ 2500 m away. Lower = encounters pop up closer to you; higher = quieter surroundings.

label: NPC visibility distance (A-Life grid)
tooltip: How far away NPC models are shown and simulated (vanilla 85 m; 'Distant Horizons' uses 150 to 250 m). Higher costs performance. Not play-tested yet.

label: Camp life
tooltip: How often stalkers in camps feel like playing the guitar, telling a joke, chatting, smoking, sleeping, resting, eating or drinking (vanilla e.g. guitar 4-6, jokes 3-6, talk 5-8 points per minute, across 25 NPC presets). Work, patrols, guard duty and emission behaviour stay vanilla. This writes a lot of small changes, so the mod scan may report overlaps with other A-Life mods. Not play-tested yet.

label: Camper detection time
tooltip: How long you may stay in one spot (5 m radius) before NPCs treat you as a camper and flank (vanilla 10 s). Not play-tested yet.

label: Offline corpse budget
tooltip: How many A-Life bodies may pile up within a lair radius (100 m) before offline decomposition kicks in (vanilla 30). Not play-tested yet.

label: Bodies alarm NPCs
tooltip: How long a fresh body counts as a threat sign for NPCs (vanilla 120 s). 0 % = they ignore bodies. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC cover distance to enemy
tooltip: The distance band NPCs prefer for a cover spot (vanilla 8-70 m from the enemy), both ends scaled together. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC cover search path
tooltip: How far NPCs will run to reach a cover spot (vanilla path length 20 m). Not play-tested yet.

label: Night darkness for NPC eyes
tooltip: The base light level NPC eyes assume by time of day (vanilla night 0.2, dawn 0.3, morning 0.6, day 1.0). 0 % = pitch black nights for NPCs; only values below 1 scale, capped at 1.0. craigduk76 reports improved night stealth at 50 % (GitHub #17). Dawn and morning also change; the exact detection effect is unmeasured.

label: Hidden damage mercy
tooltip: The game dampens damage you take in quick succession; the curve weights are 0.33-0.75 on Medium, 0.15-0.5 on Hard, 0.12-0.4 on Stalker, 1.0 on Easy. Scaled per difficulty, capped at 1.0. Direction not verified - experimental.

label: Encounters: blind dogs
tooltip: Weight of blind-dog packs. Stacks with the mutant-share slider. Bloodsuckers have no slider: the open world never rolls them (weight 0).

label: Encounters: boars
tooltip: Weight of boar packs. Stacks with the mutant-share slider. Bloodsuckers have no slider: the open world never rolls them (weight 0).

label: Encounters: chimeras
tooltip: Weight of the single-chimera encounter (veteran regions only). Stacks with the mutant-share slider. Bloodsuckers have no slider: the open world never rolls them (weight 0).

label: Random encounters: dead bodies
tooltip: Same for the share that arrives already dead (vanilla 20 to 60 % in 36 of the 95 squad entries, zero in the rest - an ambush that already happened). Capped at 100 %. Not play-tested yet.

label: Encounters: fleshes
tooltip: Weight of flesh packs. Stacks with the mutant-share slider. Bloodsuckers have no slider: the open world never rolls them (weight 0).

label: Random encounters: frequency
tooltip: How often the director rolls a new encounter around you (vanilla 60–90 s in the open world, plus a timeout after each spawn – both scale).

label: Encounters: mixed mutant packs
tooltip: Weight of the generic 'mutants' encounters, which pick any spawnable species. Stacks with the mutant-share slider. Bloodsuckers have no slider: the open world never rolls them (weight 0).

label: Random encounters: mutant share
tooltip: Weight of pure-mutant encounters against human ones (vanilla ~37 % of the open-world rolls). 0 % = no random mutant packs (lair mutants stay). Weights the game never uses (0) stay 0.

label: Random encounters: pack size (experimental)
tooltip: Scales the per-rank cap of each spawnable type (blind dogs 4–12, fleshes 2–6 ...) – our best reading of how pack size is derived, unverified. Types the director never spawns (chimera, controller, burer ...) are skipped.

label: Encounters: tushkans
tooltip: Weight of tushkan packs. Stacks with the mutant-share slider. Bloodsuckers have no slider: the open world never rolls them (weight 0).

label: Random encounters: wounded stalkers
tooltip: The game has eight scenarios that spawn wounded stalkers (friendly and hostile, single and in groups), but their share sits at 10 to 20 %. This scales that share, capped at 100 %. Squads that spawn nobody wounded in vanilla stay that way - the slider scales what exists, it does not invent wounded encounters. Not play-tested yet.

label: Faction expansion battle chance (experimental)
tooltip: Chance that a faction's offline expansion into a foreign lair turns into a battle (vanilla 50 % for all 29 factions). Offline simulation, rarely visible. Not play-tested yet.

label: Faction expansion pace (experimental)
tooltip: Scales the population manager's ALifeLairExpansionTime (vanilla 50) inversely: 200 % = factions expand twice as often, if the value is a time at all - its unit is not proven. Lair-count bands stay vanilla. Not play-tested yet.

label: Fallback spawn count
tooltip: What the director spawns when it finds no matching scenario at all (vanilla 3). Rarely used, but it is the floor under every encounter. Not play-tested yet.

label: Lairs expand toward you
tooltip: How long the simulation waits before a faction pushes a lair in your direction (vanilla 120 min). 400 % = every 30 minutes. Offline behaviour, so expect it to show up slowly. Not play-tested yet.

label: Lair population: humans
tooltip: How many stalkers a faction lair holds. Base guards (Guard lairs) stay vanilla on purpose.

label: Lair starting occupancy
tooltip: How full a lair is the first time it spawns - vanilla fills most of them only half (0.5), a few completely. 200 % = every lair starts at its full head count (capped there). Base-guard lairs stay vanilla. Not play-tested yet.

label: Lair population: mutants
tooltip: How many mutants a lair holds (all species, per player rank). Story lairs and base guards are never touched.

label: Rare lair archetypes
tooltip: Inside a lair every archetype has a draw weight: most sit at 1.0, but 170 entries are rarities at 0.2 or 0.5 (the odd sniper or close-combat specialist). This raises only those, capped at 1.0 - so the unusual ones show up more often. Archetypes at 0 stay at 0: the game means them not to appear there. Not play-tested yet.

label: Lair respawn speed
tooltip: How fast fallen lair members are replaced (vanilla 3 / 8 min, wipe 8 min). Story lairs with instant refill stay as they are.

label: NPC accuracy
tooltip: × 2 = NPCs shoot twice as precisely (smaller bullet spread).

label: NPC alertness
tooltip: How little suspicion it takes before NPCs turn their head (200), search (350), move in (500) or call allies (700 points; a gunshot is worth 700). 200 % = they react at half the suspicion. Human NPCs only.

label: NPCs walk into anomalies
tooltip: Chance that a stalker or mutant ignores the anomaly it is standing next to (vanilla 10 %, a few 40 to 50 %). Capped at 100 %. 0 % = they never blunder in. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC attack cooldown
tooltip: Difficulty multiplier on human NPC attack cooldowns (vanilla 1.0 on every difficulty). Effect scope not verified in-game - experimental.

label: NPC burst length
tooltip: Shots per burst (vanilla e.g. rifles 3-6 at long, 8-16 at short range).

label: NPC courage
tooltip: Confidence needed before human squads attack or fall back (vanilla bandits 2 / 1, monolith 0.5 / 0, others 3 / 0.5). Higher = braver. Mutants stay vanilla.

label: NPC damage memory
tooltip: How long recent damage keeps counting when NPCs weigh who hurt them (vanilla 7 s). Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC engagement range
tooltip: Distance band in which NPCs open fire with a weapon (vanilla e.g. pistols 2-25 m, rifles 15-60 m, snipers 25-100 m).

label: NPC fire pauses
tooltip: Pause between bursts (vanilla ~0.8-2.5 s) and between single shots of semi-auto weapons. 200 % = NPCs shoot half as often.

label: NPC focus on the player
tooltip: Scales the 'not the player' weight in target scoring (vanilla 0.15). Whether higher means MORE or LESS attention on you is unproven - try 0 % and 400 % and tell us. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC guaranteed-hit shots
tooltip: Shots per burst that NPCs fire with ZERO spread - the opening 'laser' fire (vanilla e.g. rifles 2-3 at long, 4-6 at short range). 0 % = every NPC shot uses normal spread; shotguns and launchers already have 0. craigduk76 reports the expected effect at 0 % (GitHub #16); NPCs can still hit you normally.

label: NPC gear quality
tooltip: Tilts each squad's weapon/armor lottery toward the pricier gear it can ALREADY carry (400 % = the best gun in a pool is 4x as likely, 25 % = rust buckets everywhere). Never adds gear a faction or rank wouldn't carry in vanilla - and their dropped loot changes accordingly.

label: NPC grenade usage
tooltip: 0 % = NPCs never throw grenades (scripted bosses keep theirs).

label: NPC hearing range
tooltip: Footsteps, shots, voices etc. Mutants are unaffected (except Supersoldiers – they use NPC hearing).

label: NPC hip-fire accuracy
tooltip: The difficulty multiplier for NPC hip fire (vanilla 1.0 everywhere). Direction assumed: higher = more precise. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC flashlight brightness & reach
tooltip: Scales the intensity and the attenuation radius of NPC flashlights (vanilla intensity 7-18 and radius 1.75-5 m, growing with the distance the beam travels). Makes NPCs easier or harder to spot at night. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC flashlight use in combat
tooltip: Chance that an NPC keeps the flashlight on while fighting, by rank (vanilla newbie 100 %, experienced 75 %, veteran 50 %, master 25 %; capped at 100 %). 0 % = never. craigduk76 observed more NPCs fighting without lights at 50 % (GitHub #18); not a measured probability test.

label: NPC flashlight beam width
tooltip: Outer cone angle of NPC flashlights (vanilla 45-80 degrees by distance, capped at 170). Not play-tested yet.

label: NPCs switch flashlights off at (hour)
tooltip: In-game hour at which NPCs turn their flashlights off (vanilla 5).

label: NPCs switch flashlights on at (hour)
tooltip: In-game hour at which NPCs turn their flashlights on (vanilla 22).

label: NPC weapon range
tooltip: Effective distance and damage drop-off of NPC weapon profiles only - the NPC-side twin of 'Weapon effective range'. Player weapons stay as they are.

label: NPC weapon rank bonus
tooltip: Raises every NPC's weapon behaviour rank by this many steps (Newbie -> Experienced -> Veteran -> Master): deadlier enemies without health sponges. Difficulty value, vanilla 0.

label: NPC reaction delay
tooltip: How long NPCs take to report threats/enemies to their squad (vanilla 2–3 s). 400 % = slow, sleepy AI; 25 % = instant alarm.

label: NPC health regen
tooltip: Passive regeneration of human NPCs (vanilla 1 HP/s, guards 20 HP/s). 0 % = same as the 'don't self-heal' box, which always wins when ticked.

label: NPC target-switch cooldown
tooltip: Minimum seconds before an NPC changes its target (vanilla 3). Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC retreat distance
tooltip: How far an NPC falls back when it decides to retreat (vanilla 8 to 25 m). Only the 32 prototypes that retreat at all are touched. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC damage before retreating
tooltip: How much damage an NPC soaks up before it pulls back (vanilla 20 to 1000 depending on the type). Lower = they break sooner. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC search time
tooltip: How long NPCs stay suspicious and keep searching (vanilla: suspicion frozen 30 s, then fades 30 points/s). 25 % = they forget you fast. craigduk76 reports longer searches at 400 % (GitHub #13). Up to 1000 % is now available; values above 400 % are not play-tested.

label: NPC stagger threshold
tooltip: Damage within 2 s that makes a human NPC flinch (vanilla 40; bosses far higher). 25 % = they stagger from almost any hit, 400 % = they barely flinch.

label: NPC vision range
tooltip: How far human NPCs (incl. the Faust fight) can see you. Korshunov & Scar boss senses stay vanilla. 10 % vision + 10 % hearing ≈ ghost mode.

label: NPC vs allies damage
tooltip: The third key of the same group: how hard NPCs hit characters friendly to you, vanilla 30 %. Raise it and escort partners die fast; lower it and they soak fire. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC vs NPC damage
tooltip: How hard stalkers hit EACH OTHER - vanilla is 70 % of normal damage on every weapon, so faction fights drag on. Does not touch what they do to you or you to them. Not play-tested yet.

label: NPC vs player damage
tooltip: How hard NPC bullets hit YOU - a per-weapon key, not the difficulty slider called 'NPC damage (to you)' further up: the two stack. Vanilla 100 % on all 150 weapon settings. 0 % = their guns cannot hurt you. Found by the key-family check in 1.35.0. Not play-tested yet.

label: Psy phantom count (Stalker difficulty)
tooltip: The Stalker difficulty spawns twice the psy phantoms (multiplier 2.0); other difficulties have no entry. Not play-tested yet.

label: Lair refill cooldown
tooltip: The A-Life policy's pause before a wiped-out lair is refilled (vanilla 360 s after a full wipe, 120 s after a partial one). 25 % = lairs come back four times as fast. Not play-tested yet.

label: Lair refill distance
tooltip: How far from you a lair must be before it refills (vanilla 200-250 m band). Not play-tested yet.

label: A-Life squad expansion (experimental)
tooltip: How quickly the urge to send out expansion squads grows in 16 NPC need presets (vanilla 6-10 points per minute for humans, zombies 1-3, mutants 7-11; a squad leaves at 100). More squads roaming = more CPU load. Not play-tested yet.

label: Crouch stealth
tooltip: How much crouching and crawling hide you from eyes AND ears (vanilla: crouched you are 25 % less visible and much quieter). 200 % = twice as hard to notice while crouched.

label: Flashlight gives you away
tooltip: How strongly your own flashlight fills NPC vision (cone 10 m / 15° in vanilla). 0 % = the beam never reveals you.

label: Movement noise
tooltip: Noise of walking, running and sprinting (vanilla 0.6 / 0.8 / 1.0). 0 % = silent feet; crouch noise has its own slider above.

label: Bad-weather stealth
tooltip: How much fog, rain and thunder blind and deafen NPCs (vanilla: fog -30 % sight / -60 % hearing, thunder -20 % / -70 %). 0 % = weather changes nothing, 300 % = storms make you nearly invisible.

label: Simultaneous special attacks
tooltip: Abilities and knockdowns (vanilla 1 at a time).

label: Simultaneous grenade throwers
tooltip: Vanilla 1 at a time.

label: Simultaneous melee attackers
tooltip: Vanilla 5 on every difficulty.

label: Simultaneous suppressive fire
tooltip: Vanilla 2 to 5 depending on difficulty and rank.

label: Weapon-out warnings before guards turn hostile
tooltip: How often guards warn you to holster before they attack (vanilla 3). Not play-tested yet.

label: Time between weapon-out warnings
tooltip: Vanilla 10 s between warnings. Not play-tested yet.

label: Wounded-state cooldown
tooltip: Seconds before the same NPC can go down wounded again (vanilla 300). Very low values = NPCs drop again and again. Not play-tested yet.

label: Wounded NPCs: chance to recover
tooltip: When a human NPC goes down wounded, this is the chance (vanilla 70 %) that they heal over time instead of bleeding out. 0 % = every downed NPC bleeds out. Not play-tested yet.

label: Wounded NPC health regen
tooltip: Health per second a wounded NPC regains (vanilla 5). 0 % = none. Not play-tested yet.

label: Wounded heal threshold (experimental)
tooltip: The game's HpThresholdToHealWound (vanilla 35). Either 'healable below this many HP' or 'wakes up with this many HP' - the direction is not proven. Not play-tested yet.

label: Zombie spread penalty
tooltip: Zombified stalkers shoot with an extra 30 of spread on top of the weapon's own (vanilla, all 75 NPC weapon profiles). 0 % = zombies aim as well as anyone else. Not play-tested yet.

label: Fall damage
tooltip: 0 % = no fall damage.

label: Max health
tooltip: Logarithmic slider: fine steps near vanilla 100, up to 100000 for god-mode runs (a user reports the game accepts it). Medkits heal a fixed amount (basic medkit 70 HP), so at very high health raise 'Medkit & bandage healing' too.

label: Passive health regen (HP/s)
tooltip: Vanilla: no passive regen. NPCs use 1 HP/s.

label: Run & sprint speed
tooltip: Animations and footstep sounds can't scale with speed (engine limitation) – subtle changes feel best.

label: Jump
tooltip: Since 1.28.0 this also scales the stamina lost on landing after a jump or fall (vanilla coefficient 0.5).

label: All traders have unlimited money
tooltip: Switches the remaining finite wallets to unlimited (most are already unlimited in vanilla).

label: Show traders, technicians, medics and guides on the map
tooltip: 80 NPCs already carry a map symbol in the game data - 34 traders, 18 technicians, 14 guides, 14 medics - but their display flag is off; only eight are shown in vanilla. This turns the flag on for exactly those 80. Nobody new is added, and NPCs without a symbol are untouched. Not play-tested yet.

label: Traders don't buy weapons or armor (hardcore)
tooltip: Adds Weapon and Armor to every trader's buy restrictions (existing restrictions stay). Like 'TradersDontBuyWeaponsArmor'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Trader restock time
section: Stock (what traders have on the shelf)
tooltip: How long traders take to refresh their stock (vanilla: 8 h to 7 days depending on the trader; day-based traders can't go below 1 day).

label: Traders buy gear from durability
tooltip: 0 % = traders buy weapons/armor in any condition (vanilla: 40 %).

label: Trader money
tooltip: Scales the coupon wallet traders pay you from. Honest note: most traders (59 of 73) already have unlimited money in vanilla – this affects the finite wallets (bartenders etc.). Since 1.28.0 it also scales the coupon amounts carried on the NPC structs themselves (22 of them, precedence unverified).

label: Trader stock amount
section: Stock (what traders have on the shelf)
tooltip: Scales the quantities on offer (ammo boxes, medkit stacks ...). Weapons and armor are single items – they only multiply from 150 % up, like loot.

label: Trader stock variety
section: Stock (what traders have on the shelf)
tooltip: Each catalog item has a chance to be in stock after a restock. Higher = fuller shelves (chance is capped at 100 %), lower = patchier stock. What a trader CAN carry stays their vanilla catalog – honest limit: this tool does not add new items to traders.

label: Upgrades need no blueprint
tooltip: Upgrades that normally need a blueprint item become available without it. Technicians still only service the gear they are scripted for. Both boxes above = 'Unrestricted Upgrades'.

label: No upgrade tiers (skip earlier tiers)
tooltip: Tier 2/3 upgrades no longer require the earlier tier first. All three boxes = 'Unrestricted Upgrades - NoTiers'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Take both of mutually exclusive upgrades
tooltip: Upgrade branches that normally exclude each other (barrel A or barrel B ...) can all be installed. Same idea as the 'Take Both Upgrades' Nexus mod. Not play-tested yet.

label: Recoil reduction from upgrades
tooltip: Multiplies the recoil reduction of weapon upgrades and attachments (vanilla -5 % to -30 %), capped at -100 %. 2000 % = any recoil upgrade removes the kick entirely. Community-proven on patch 2.0 (same route as the 'Dead Steady' mod).

label: Scope handling penalties
tooltip: The aim-time and ADS-movement penalties scopes carry (vanilla +7 to +20 % aim time, -5 to -10 % movement). 0 % = none. Not play-tested yet.

label: Scope magnification
tooltip: Scales the zoom of every scope class (vanilla 2x -43 %, 3x -51 %, 4x -60 %, 8x -70 % of the FOV; capped at -90 %). Not play-tested yet.

label: Handling upgrades (aim time, ADS move, sway, draw, recovery, capacity)
Flashlight stays bright in dialogue
tooltip: Vanilla dims your flashlight to 52.5 % while you talk; this keeps it at 100 %. Not play-tested yet.

label: Improved vaulting (community preset)
tooltip: Restores the tuned vaulting of the pre-2.0 vault mod (broken since the game's 2.0 update): steeper approach angles, vault from farther away, higher obstacles, more generous landing. Player only - NPCs keep vanilla vaulting. Not play-tested on 2.0.x yet.

label: Look straight down
tooltip: Vanilla stops the camera at 80° below the horizon; this allows 90°. Confirmed in-game by craigduk76 on 1.35.0 (GitHub #11). Its former neighbour 'Free look on ladders' was removed in 1.36.0 in the same test: the two ladder keys sit in the same file and did nothing.

label: Map: show all region names from the start
tooltip: The 23 region names start hidden in vanilla. Like the 'all location names on the map' mod. Not play-tested yet.

label: Skif can't be knocked down
tooltip: Mutant charges and blasts no longer throw you to the ground (vanilla: they can). Like 'CantBeKnockedDown'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Never limp after landings
tooltip: Pushes both landing thresholds to 1000x vanilla, so no landing triggers the limp any more (overrides the slider above). Not play-tested yet.

label: Turn off mouse smoothing
tooltip: Unreal smooths mouse input by default and the game's options cannot switch it off. This writes Stalker2/Config/UserInput.ini into the pak - the only thing this tool builds that is not a game data patch, so the mod scan cannot see conflicts with another mod shipping the same file. Removing the pak removes it again. Not play-tested yet.

label: Turn off view acceleration
tooltip: The second flag in the same file: the camera speeding up while you keep turning. Same caveats as above. Not play-tested yet.

label: No slowdown in water
tooltip: Removes the turn-rate and movement penalties while wading (like 'NoSluggishWater'). Stamina drain in deep water stays. Not play-tested yet.

label: Skip the intro video
tooltip: Cuts the opening video's start link in the quest graph (same route as 'SkipIntroCutscene'). Only matters for a new game. Not play-tested yet.

label: Sleep whenever you like (no 'not tired enough')
tooltip: Vanilla lets you sleep only from 50 % tiredness. Not play-tested yet.

label: Allow sleeping during emissions
tooltip: Vanilla forbids it. Not play-tested yet.

label: Start vaulting while sprinting (experimental)
tooltip: Sets the game's StartWithSprintPressed flag. Its exact in-game effect is NOT verified yet - it reads like 'vault can trigger while sprint is held'. Try it and tell us.

label: Air control while jumping
tooltip: How much you can steer mid-air (vanilla coefficient 0.1, capped at 1.0). Not play-tested yet.

label: Autosave interval
tooltip: Minutes between timed autosaves (vanilla 10).

label: Backward & sideways speed
tooltip: Walking backwards is 50 % of forward speed in vanilla, running backwards 43 %, crouched 47-54 %, diagonal 72-75 %. Capped at forward speed. Not play-tested yet.

label: Bleeding per hit
tooltip: Bleeding points a wounding hit adds (vanilla 10 on a bar of 100). 0 % = hits never make you bleed. Not play-tested yet.

label: Bleeding from non-penetrating hits
tooltip: Chance and amount of bleeding from hits your armor stops (vanilla modifiers 1.0). 0 % = only hits that get through make you bleed. Not play-tested yet.

label: Bleeding stops by itself
tooltip: How fast bleeding fades without a bandage (vanilla 0.3 per second). Not play-tested yet.

label: Camera slowdown from hazards
tooltip: How much your view is slowed while a chemical anomaly, barbed wire or a flycatcher has hold of you (vanilla -60 %, -80 %, -70 %). 0 % = no slowdown at all. The bloodsucker roar uses a different key with an unknown unit and is left alone. Not play-tested yet.

label: Ladder climb speed
tooltip: How fast Skif climbs ladders (vanilla coefficient 0.6) - since 1.28.0 including the five ladder animation play-rates. Not play-tested yet.

label: Corpse dragging speed
tooltip: Speed while dragging a body (vanilla 60 % of normal, capped at 100 %); since 1.28.0 the time to grab a body (vanilla 2 s) shrinks the same way. Not play-tested yet.

label: Crouch vignette
tooltip: The dark screen edges while crouching (vanilla intensity 0.6). 0 % = none, like 'Remove Crouch Vignette'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Cutscene field of view (unverified)
tooltip: Vanilla 90. Not play-tested yet - and its sibling 'Dialog field of view' was removed in 1.36.0 after a player found it had no effect (GitHub #10); this key sits right next to it, so expect the same until someone reports otherwise.

label: Damage screen effects
tooltip: The red directional hit flash and the burn, steam, chemical, electric, darkness and quicksilver overlays (15 post-effect processors, vanilla intensity 1.0). 0 % also removes the visual warning inside chemical fields. Not play-tested yet.

label: Default field of view (unverified)
tooltip: The game's default gameplay FOV (vanilla 90). The FOV setting in the game's own options most likely wins; this only changes the default. Not play-tested yet, and see the cutscene slider above for the caveat.

label: Maximum talk distance only
tooltip: Extends only the maximum conversation distance on the player and human NPCs, using each one's installed value. 100 % = unchanged. Leave Talk distance (minimum & maximum) at 100 % to keep the vanilla minimum; if both controls are changed, their maximum-distance factors multiply. Existing profiles retain their previous behavior. Requested in GitHub #10; this separate maximum-only setting has not been play-tested.

label: Talk distance (minimum & maximum)
tooltip: How close you have to be to start a conversation (vanilla 1.3 m). The 'Social Distancing' idea from Nexus. Up to 1.35.0 only Skif carried the new distance and a player found it did nothing (GitHub #10) - every one of the 1608 human NPCs carries its own copy, and the game evidently reads theirs. Since 1.36.0 they all get it too. Confirmed by craigduk76 on 1.37.1 at 200 % (GitHub #10). Both minimum and maximum distance scale: standing too close can prevent interaction. Leave this at 100 % and use Maximum talk distance only to extend reach while keeping the minimum unchanged.

label: Energy drink tolerance (Cost of Hope)
tooltip: How many energy drinks Skif takes before overuse and tolerance effects kick in (vanilla overuse 1000, tolerance 2500 points). Not play-tested yet.

label: Hands-free zoom (right mouse, no weapon)
tooltip: How far the view zooms when you hold aim with empty hands (vanilla FOV factor 0.8; lower = stronger zoom, Ace's CoreVariables list suggests 0.55 = 70 %). Capped between 0.2 and 1.0. Not play-tested yet.

label: Interaction reach (pick up, loot, containers)
tooltip: How far away you can pick up items, open stashes and containers and loot bodies (vanilla 2 m; bodies 0.65 m, scaled the same way) - since 1.28.0 plus the wide-trace, auto-interaction, mutant-harvest and body-drag ranges. Not play-tested yet.

label: Jog below stamina
tooltip: Below this share of stamina Skif can only jog (vanilla 50 %). 0 % = sprint until the bar is empty. Not play-tested yet.

label: Limping speed (wounded)
tooltip: Movement speed while limping (vanilla 50 % of normal, capped at 100 %). Not play-tested yet.

label: Limp threshold after hard landings
tooltip: How hard a landing must be before Skif starts limping (vanilla thresholds 25 for the short limp, 65 for the longer one; × 2 = twice as hard). Not play-tested yet.

label: Look speed, horizontal
tooltip: Turning speed left and right. Vanilla is 40 on the player and 50 in the core config - so you turn a third faster sideways than you look up and down, and the game's own sensitivity setting moves both together and cannot change that ratio. Both places are scaled the same. Not play-tested yet.

label: Look speed, vertical
tooltip: Looking up and down (vanilla 30 in both places). Set this to about 133 % to match the horizontal speed. Not play-tested yet.

label: Map: location reveal distance
tooltip: How close you must come before a place appears on the PDA map and counts as explored (vanilla mostly 100 m / 20 m, scaled together) - since 1.28.0 plus the three global HUD marker distances (300 / 30 / 20 m). Not play-tested yet.

label: Combat music lingers
tooltip: How long an attack keeps counting as combat, i.e. how long the music keeps playing after the shooting stops (vanilla 25 s). Not play-tested yet.

label: Combat music threshold
tooltip: How much nearby danger it takes before combat music starts (vanilla 20 points; one ordinary stalker counts 10, a heavy one 20, a dog 7 - so two normal enemies trigger it). Higher = music only in big fights. Not play-tested yet.

label: Psy recovery
tooltip: How fast psy damage recovers (vanilla 1 per second). Not play-tested yet.

label: Quicksave overwrite window
tooltip: For how long a new quicksave overwrites the previous slot instead of starting a new one (vanilla 5 min). 0 = every quicksave gets its own slot, up to the quick save slot limit above. Not play-tested yet.

label: Natural radiation decay
tooltip: How fast accumulated radiation fades on its own (vanilla 0.05 per second). 0 % = only pills and vodka help. Not play-tested yet.

label: Health regen delay
tooltip: Seconds after the last hit before health regeneration starts (vanilla 5). Pairs with the passive regen slider above. Not play-tested yet.

label: Autosave slots
tooltip: How many timed autosaves are kept (vanilla 10).

label: Manual save slots
tooltip: How many manual saves a campaign may hold before the game makes you delete one (vanilla 31). The 'Unlimited Saves' idea from Nexus. Not play-tested yet.

label: Quick save slots
tooltip: How many quick saves are kept (vanilla 3).

label: Sleep fade time
tooltip: The fade to black (vanilla 1.5 s) and the black screen (3.5 s) when sleeping. 0 % = instant. Not play-tested yet.

label: Minimum sleep
tooltip: The shortest sleep the game allows (vanilla 7 h). Not play-tested yet.

label: Sober-up speed
tooltip: How fast drunkenness wears off (vanilla 1 per second). Confirmed in-game by craigduk76 at 25 % on 1.35.0 and at 1 %, including eventual sobriety (GitHub #12). 1 % slows the configured recovery rate to one hundredth of vanilla.

label: Starting money (new game only)
tooltip: Coupons Skif starts a NEW game with (vanilla 0). Has no effect on an existing save. Not play-tested yet.

label: Stealth kill reach
tooltip: How close you must be behind an NPC for a stealth kill (vanilla 1.8 m). Not play-tested yet.

label: Vault approach angle
tooltip: How far off-center you may face an obstacle and still vault it (capped at 180°).

label: Vault trigger distance
tooltip: From how far away vaulting triggers (vanilla is very strict - the old vault mod used roughly 750 %).

label: Max vault height
tooltip: How high an obstacle you can still vault or climb over (vanilla detection limit ~1.3 m). All vault sliders stack on top of the preset below when both are used.

label: Vault landing tolerance
tooltip: How forgiving the landing check is: farther, steeper and lower landing spots count (three game values scaled together).

label: Vault min obstacle height
tooltip: Below 100 % even small crates trigger vaulting; above, only taller obstacles do.

label: Vault-over max thickness
tooltip: How deep/thick an obstacle may be and still be cleared in one vault-over. The old vault mod HALVED this, preferring quick climbs onto thick objects.

label: Vault-over landing distance
tooltip: How far beyond the obstacle you land when vaulting over it (the old mod used 500 % - clean jumps over fences instead of stopping on them).

label: Time speed while the quick wheel is open
tooltip: The game slows to 30 % while the item selector is open (vanilla). 100 % = real time, 5 % = almost paused. Not play-tested yet.

label: GunMark_SP  ·  „Mark I EMR“ / ADS move speed
GunMark_SP  ·  „Mark I EMR“ / ADS aim-in speed
Gun_Lummox_AR_GS  ·  „Valik Lummox's AKM-74S“ / ADS move speed
Gun_Lummox_AR_GS  ·  „Valik Lummox's AKM-74S“ / ADS aim-in speed
Gun_Unknown_AR_GS  ·  „Unknown Stalker's AR416“ / ADS move speed
Gun_Unknown_AR_GS  ·  „Unknown Stalker's AR416“ / ADS aim-in speed
Every weapon keeps a round in the chamber
tooltip: 65 of the 92 weapons already give you one extra round after reloading; this brings the other 27 in line. Not play-tested yet.

label: Turn aim assist off for gamepads
Turn aim assist off for the mouse
Inventory stat bars follow your changes
tooltip: The damage/range/fire-rate bars in the inventory are decoration: the game never computes them from the real values, they are fixed numbers on every weapon. Tick this and they move with your sliders, per weapon and per category. Accuracy and handling are left alone - they mix dispersion, recoil and weight, and there is no honest formula for them. Cosmetic only, it changes no damage. Not play-tested yet.

label: ADS zoom
tooltip: How much the view zooms in when aiming down sights (vanilla FOV factor 0.92 for most weapons, 0.83 for some). 0 % = no zoom at all, 200 % = twice the vanilla zoom. Scopes keep their own magnification. Not play-tested yet.

label: ADS movement speed
tooltip: How fast you move while aiming down sights (vanilla varies 58–150 % of run speed per weapon).

label: Aim & crouch steadiness
tooltip: How much aiming down the sights and crouching calm the weapon (experimental). Vanilla: crouching takes 15 % off the recoil, and on 71 weapons aiming removes the spread entirely. Capped at 'removes it completely' - the game data has nothing stronger, and what it would do with more is anyone's guess. Not play-tested yet.

label: ADS aim-in speed
tooltip: How fast the weapon comes up into the sights, incl. offset and lean aiming (vanilla ~0.5 s). 200 % = twice as snappy. Not play-tested yet – watch for aim animation glitches and report back.

label: Skipped shooting animations (experimental)
tooltip: The game's own ShootingAnimationNumberToSkip, vanilla 0 on every weapon. It is the only config key that touches the shooting animation at all - speed and sound live in baked assets no config patch can reach. If you raise a weapon's fire rate and the animation lags behind, try 1 (skip every other animation) or 2. The animation gets choppier, but it stops trailing the shots. Read from the key name only, never play-tested - tell us what you see.

label: Breath-hold drain
tooltip: 0 % = hold breath forever while aiming.

label: Bullet drop
tooltip: How far bullets fall over distance (vanilla drop height 170 on every weapon class). 0 % = flat trajectory, like 'Fully Unlocked Ballistics'. NPC bullets are unchanged. Not play-tested yet.

label: Bullet wall penetration
tooltip: Chance that a bullet carries on through what it hits (vanilla 0 to 1.0 depending on the round; rounds at 0 stay at 0). Capped at 100 %. Not play-tested yet.

label: Bullet penetration depth
tooltip: How thick a wall a bullet can still come through (vanilla 150 to 300 on the 16 projectile types). The slider above decides IF it punches through, this one how far. Not play-tested yet.

label: Bullet max range
tooltip: How far a projectile flies before it is removed (vanilla 100000 for every round - 1 km). Rarely the limit you notice, but it is the hard ceiling. Not play-tested yet.

label: Bullet speed
tooltip: Flight speed of the 11 bullet types (vanilla 20000 to 42000). Gauss, RPG and grenade launcher rounds are untouched. Faster = less lead on moving targets. Not play-tested yet.

label: Weapon wear per butt strike
tooltip: Every butt strike costs the weapon 5 durability in vanilla. 0 % = bash crates for free, like 'The weapon doesn't break when used to strike with the butt'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Ammo in dropped weapons
tooltip: How much ammunition sits in the weapon of a dead NPC (vanilla 1 to 10 rounds). Weapons whose value is unset in vanilla are left alone. Whole rounds. Not play-tested yet.

label: Weapon draw & holster speed
tooltip: How fast a weapon is raised and put away (the game's ShowEquipmentTime and HideEquipmentTime, vanilla 1.0 on every weapon). 200 % = half the time. Unlike the reload slider this one also covers the Deluxe and Pre-order weapons. The same animation caveat applies: the timing value changes, the animation may not follow. Not play-tested yet.

label: Damage at extreme range
tooltip: Past the drop-off distance a shot keeps only a fraction of its damage - vanilla 10 to 60 % depending on the gun. This is the floor under that, capped at 100 % (full damage at any range). Armour penetration at range moves with it, but it already sits at 100 % in vanilla, so there only values below 100 % change anything. The range slider above moves the distances, this one the damage left behind them. Not play-tested yet.

label: Hip-fire stance effect
tooltip: How much your stance changes hip fire. Vanilla: crouching takes 0.2 off the spread, jumping adds 0.3. 0 % = stance makes no difference from the hip, 200 % doubles both. The aiming counterpart is the slider above. Not play-tested yet.

label: Weapon jam chance
tooltip: How often a worn weapon jams. Vanilla runs from 4.5 to 15 depending on the gun, and this scales each one; 0 % = weapons never jam at all. The condition at which jamming starts is left alone. Stacks with the difficulty jamming multiplier. Not play-tested yet.

label: Jam clearing speed
tooltip: How fast a jam is cleared (vanilla 4 to 5.5 s per weapon). 200 % = half the time. Not play-tested yet.

label: Magazine size
tooltip: Scales weapon base capacity AND all magazine attachments (launchers never drop below 1 round). Per category or per weapon: 'Magazine size' is the tenth factor in the trees below.

label: Melee range (knife & butt strike)
tooltip: How far the knife and the butt strike reach (vanilla 1.6 m for both). The 'Increased Melee Range' idea from Nexus. Not play-tested yet.

label: Movement effect on aim
tooltip: How much walking and running spoil your aim (vanilla adds 0.1 to 1.0 to the spread, depending on the weapon). 0 % = moving costs you no accuracy at all. Not play-tested yet.

label: Pistol slot accepts
tooltip: Lets SMGs, shotguns or any weapon sit in the sidearm slot; the two main slots keep taking every weapon. The 'SMG in pistol slot' and 'Any weapon as sidearm' mods. Not play-tested yet.

label: Weapon recoil
tooltip: Scales the kick per shot (RecoilRadius). 0 % = no kick. The per-shot pattern shape is a game asset and keeps its direction, only its size follows the slider. Not play-tested yet - report back.

label: Recoil pattern reset
tooltip: How long you have to stop shooting before the recoil pattern starts from the top again (vanilla 0.3 s, a few weapons 1 to 5 s). The pattern's DIRECTION lives in a packed asset and cannot be changed from config - only this pause and the strength. Not play-tested yet.

label: Recoil & spread recovery
tooltip: How quickly the weapon settles back down after a shot. Recoil and spread each have their own recovery time in vanilla (0.25 to 0.8 s); 200 % halves both. Not play-tested yet.

label: Reload speed
tooltip: Scales every reload-time multiplier the game keeps per weapon and magazine (vanilla 1.0 everywhere, the fields the official Zone Kit guide points at). 200 % = half the time. Edition weapons (Deluxe/Pre-order) stay vanilla. NOT play-tested yet - the animation may or may not follow, report back.

label: Shooting camera shake
tooltip: How much the camera shakes when YOU fire (every weapon's own shake entry, vanilla scale 1.0). 0 % = none, like the 'No Screenshake' mod. Being hit is the separate 'Hit camera shake' slider on the Combat tab. Not play-tested yet.

label: Weapon spread (bullet dispersion)
tooltip: 0 % = laser accuracy (hip fire, aiming and first shot).

label: Spread build-up
tooltip: How much the spread widens while you keep firing (vanilla up to 1.5, and 39 weapons have no build-up at all - those stay that way). 0 % = the spread never grows during a burst. Recoil has no build-up in vanilla, so this only touches spread. Not play-tested yet.

label: Scoped aim sway
tooltip: 0 % = steady scopes. Iron-sight sway is animation-driven and not cfg-tweakable.

label: Weapon bleeding
tooltip: Bleeding chance and intensity your shots inflict. 0 % = your bullets never cause bleeding.

label: Weapon noise
tooltip: How loud your weapon is - what NPCs actually hear (vanilla 0.6 to 0.8; silenced cases sit at 0 and stay there). 0 % = nobody hears your shots. This is the missing half of the stealth sliders, which so far only changed how well NPCs hear. Confirmed at 300 % by craigduk76: an unsuppressed AK alerted NPCs in a spot where it previously did not (GitHub #15).

label: Weapon effective range
tooltip: Scales effective fire distance and damage drop-off start/length together.

label: Equipped items are weightless
tooltip: Worn armor and held weapons don't count toward inventory weight.

label: No overweight penalty at all
tooltip: Removes the speed/stamina penalties entirely (between penalty start and hard limit) - and, since 1.28.0, the small stamina drain from carried weight below the penalty line as well.

label: Quest items weigh nothing
tooltip: Sets the weight of every quest item to 0 (most of them weigh something, up to 25 kg). Helps with quest items that get stuck in the inventory.

label: Food & medicine stack size
tooltip: How many of one food, drink or medical item fit in a single inventory slot (vanilla 999 for all 24 of them). Honest note: 999 is a limit you will almost never reach - ammunition is the one that actually bites, and it has its own slider in the Ammo tab. Not play-tested yet.

label: Inventory action speed
tooltip: How long using something from the inventory takes (vanilla 2.5 to 5 s). 200 % = half the time. Not play-tested yet.

label: Inventory space per item
tooltip: How many grid cells an item takes up (vanilla 1x1 for small things up to 6x3 for a rifle). 50 % roughly halves every footprint; nothing ever drops below one cell. Whole cells only, so small items may not change at all. Not play-tested yet.

label: Overweight penalty starts at
tooltip: Below this weight: no slowdown at all. Stages scale up to the hard limit.

label: Item weight
tooltip: 0 % = selected categories weigh nothing.

label: Uncommon artifact caches actually drop (experimental)
tooltip: One world loot group, 'ArtifactUncommon', has nine places on the map but all 20 of its entries carry weight 0 - so those caches come up empty. This gives each entry weight 1. Whether the game rolls such a group at all is unproven. Not play-tested yet.

label: Artifacts are visible without a detector
tooltip: 147 of the 154 artifacts require a detector to be shown at all; this clears that flag on those 147 and leaves the seven that already don't need one alone. Confirmed in-game by Molkerr on 1.35.0 (GitHub #9). Whether they then show from any distance or still within each artifact's own radius is not measured.

label: Artifacts don't hop away
tooltip: 146 of the 154 artifacts jump away when you get close; this switches that off. The eight that already stay put (the weird DLC ones and two quest artifacts) are left alone. Confirmed in-game by Molkerr on 1.35.0 (GitHub #9).

label: Artifact bonus labels follow your changes
tooltip: Shows the nearest native strength tier after global and individual bonus changes; ties use the lower tier. Zero bonuses are hidden. These are approximate labels, not exact numbers. Radiation shielding tiers and unusual artifacts are separate. Off keeps the original labels. Not play-tested yet.

label: Exact condition (no random spread)
tooltip: Every dropped weapon spawns at exactly the value above (or at its own vanilla average if the slider is untouched).

label: Instant teleports (no fade to black)
tooltip: Every teleport effect (guides, quests) becomes instant (like 'InstaTeleports'). Not play-tested yet.

label: Anomaly damage: gravity
tooltip: Carousel, Razor, Expulsion, Diamond … (PSY anomalies drain psy, not health – no slider).

label: Anomaly damage (all types)
tooltip: Global difficulty multiplier – stacks with the per-type sliders below.

label: Artifacts per anomaly field
tooltip: How many artifacts a field hands out per spawn (vanilla 1). Which artifacts a field CAN spawn stays its vanilla list.

label: Artifact effect strength
tooltip: Scales what artifacts do on your belt – positive effects AND side effects alike (radiation has its own slider below).

label: Artifact hops per series (experimental)
tooltip: How many hops in a row before the artifact rests (vanilla 3, 5, 7 or 9 depending on the artifact; the two that never hop stay at zero). Whole numbers, never below one. Not play-tested yet.

label: Artifact hop distance (experimental)
tooltip: How far and high one hop carries the artifact (vanilla 15 m distance, 1 m height, force 15). Lower = it barely gets away from you. Not play-tested yet.

label: Artifact hop pause (experimental)
tooltip: Pause between two hop series (vanilla 15 to 45 s depending on the artifact) and, since 1.35.0, the shorter pause between the single hops of one series (3 or 6 s). Higher = they sit still longer. Not play-tested yet.

label: Artifact keep-away distance (experimental)
tooltip: How far a hopping artifact tries to stay away from you (vanilla 10 m, plus the 6 m at which hopping starts at all). Whether lower really means easier to catch is untested. Not play-tested yet.

label: Artifact radiation side-effect
tooltip: 0 % = artifacts emit no radiation at all.

label: Artifact 'Radius' value (unproven)
tooltip: Every artifact carries a Radius of 40 cm. We built this slider believing that is what 'Less Shy Artifacts' changes - since then we have read that mod's files, and it does something else entirely: it raises the DETECTOR's ShowArtifactRadius. So what this key does is genuinely unknown, and the slider may do nothing. If you want artifacts to show up from further away, use 'Detector & scanner range' in the World tab instead - that is the key the mod actually uses. Not play-tested yet.

label: Rare artifact bias
tooltip: Shifts the rarity roll toward Uncommon/Rare/Epic at Common's expense. Ranks that can't roll Rare/Epic in vanilla (e.g. Newbie) still won't.

label: Artifact respawn speed
tooltip: How fast fields cool down before the next artifact (vanilla mostly 3-15, some 60-120). Fields with no cooldown stay as they are.

label: Artifact spawn chance
tooltip: Chance that anomaly fields spawn an artifact (vanilla 25–40 %, capped at 100 %).

label: Barbed wire damage
tooltip: Damage, bleeding and armor wear from barbed wire (vanilla 10 damage, 25 bleeding points, 5 armor damage, 10 % bleeding chance; both fence types). 0 % = wire is harmless. Not play-tested yet.

label: Clicker anomaly strength
tooltip: The flashbang-like Clicker anomaly: number of flashes (vanilla 20) and burn per hit (vanilla 70). 0 % = one harmless flash, like 'FlashbangAnomalyNerf'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Cloud opacity
tooltip: Vanilla 0.7, capped at 1. Not play-tested yet.

label: Cloud speed
tooltip: Vanilla 1. Not play-tested yet.

label: Consumable effect duration
tooltip: How long running consumable effects last (energy drink 45 s, Hercules 5 min, cinnamon, vodka/psy-block ...). Instant effects (healing, bleeding stop, anti-rad, 1-2 s) are untouched on purpose.

label: Consumable strength
tooltip: Medkits, bandages, food, drinks: healing, bleeding/radiation removal, stamina etc. Penalties (drunkness, spoiled food) stay vanilla.

label: Containers refill after
tooltip: Respawn time of every container type (vanilla 0 = never). Experimental: in-game hours, could refill world crates and safes. Not play-tested yet.

label: Corpse distance
tooltip: The radii the corpse system works with: bodies go offline beyond 100 m, the time and count rules apply within 50 / 30 m, overpopulated bodies are destroyed beyond 300 m - all scaled together (the game stores the first three squared, the tool squares the factor). Not play-tested yet.

label: A-Life corpse hard cap
tooltip: Global ceiling of bodies the A-Life keeps at all (vanilla 1500). Not play-tested yet.

label: Max bodies near you
tooltip: How many bodies the game keeps around you before it starts removing the oldest (vanilla 10). Higher costs performance. Not play-tested yet.

label: Bodies stay
tooltip: How long dead bodies remain (vanilla 30 min near you, 15 min once seen, 5 min once looted). Since 1.28.0 also the 3 s grace after you look away and the offline coefficient. Like 'Corpse Despawn Time Increased'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Day length
tooltip: How long a full day-night cycle takes in real time (vanilla: one game day per real hour). 200 % = two hours per day, the day/night ratio stays vanilla.

label: Day starts at
tooltip: The hour the game counts as day (vanilla 6; dawn 4 moves along if needed). Which systems read these phases is not verified - experimental.

label: Detector & scanner range
tooltip: Artifact detectors (Echo, Bear, Veles, Gilka), the anomaly beeper and the searchpoint scanner.

label: Dropped weapon condition
tooltip: AVERAGE condition of weapons found on bodies and in the world (vanilla ~37.5 % for primary weapons). The game keeps rolling randomly around it, exactly like vanilla – at 80 % most drops land between ~67 and ~93 %. Armor, helmets, artifacts and trader stock stay vanilla.

label: Dusk & dawn length
tooltip: How long the light takes to fade between day and night (vanilla 2 game hours). Not play-tested yet.

label: Emission frequency
tooltip: How often emissions build up (quest-controlled no-emission zones stay untouched).

label: Emission duration
tooltip: Stretches the whole emission timeline together - warning siren, shockwave, deadly phase and aftermath (vanilla ~1 min warning + ~1 min active). Story emissions keep their scripted timing.

label: Evening starts at
tooltip: The hour the game counts as evening (vanilla 20). Experimental.

label: Explosive containers durability (experimental)
tooltip: How much damage gas cylinders, canisters and fuel barrels take before they blow (vanilla threshold 20 to 50). 25 % = they pop from almost any hit - which also means scripted set pieces can go off earlier than intended. Not play-tested yet.

label: Fast travel when overweight
tooltip: Vanilla guides refuse to travel while you are overweight ('Full' lock). 'Partial' and 'No lock' are the two other values the game engine knows. Not play-tested yet.

label: Geiger counter volume
tooltip: How loud the geiger crackle gets in a field (vanilla 0.2 to 0.8, capped at 1). Not play-tested yet.

label: Guide delay
tooltip: The GuideDelay value every guide carries (vanilla 120). Its exact meaning in-game is not verified; 0 % = no delay. The cost is on the Economy tab. Not play-tested yet.

label: Medkit & bandage healing
tooltip: Health restored by medical items only (medkits and bandages, vanilla 20–100 HP) – food and drink healing is not affected. Stacks with Consumable strength: both at 200 % = 4× healing.

label: Hunger rate
tooltip: 0 % = never get hungry.

label: Dropped items stay
tooltip: How long items lying in the world remain (vanilla 1 h untouched, 3 h otherwise). Not play-tested yet.

label: Loot amount (NPCs, containers, world)
tooltip: Only ammo and part of the food & medicine lists come as real stacks and scale smoothly. Almost everything else (detectors, grenades, artifacts, weapons, armor, mutant parts) is one item per slot: unchanged below 150 %, then 2 from 150 %, 3 from 275 % and so on.

label: Loot re-roll radius on rank-up
tooltip: When your rank goes up, the game re-rolls the loot in containers and stashes within 400 m (vanilla). Larger = more of the world refreshes at once. Not play-tested yet.

label: Loot re-roll delay on rank-up
tooltip: How long the game waits after the rank-up before it re-rolls (vanilla 10 s). Not play-tested yet.

label: Moon brightness
tooltip: Vanilla 1.046. 0 % = pitch-black nights. Not play-tested yet.

label: Push and kick force (experimental)
tooltip: How hard you shove physics props and bodies out of the way (vanilla 20 for a lab jar up to 27000 for an ammo crate, 3500 for a corpse). High values can throw objects around wildly. Not play-tested yet.

label: Radiation dose per second
tooltip: How fast radiation fields fill your bar (vanilla 1 / 3 / 6 points per second for light, medium and strong fields; the strong ones fill it in about 17 s). Stacks with 'Radiation accumulation' above. The deadly map-border zones are never touched. Not play-tested yet.

label: Radiation screen filter
tooltip: Strength of the green screen filter inside radiation fields (vanilla 0.45 to 0.75, capped at 1). 0 % = no filter - watch the geiger counter instead. Not play-tested yet.

label: Radiation accumulation
tooltip: × 0 = no radiation buildup.

label: Rain & storm frequency
tooltip: Weight of rainy/stormy/thunder weather in the rotation. 0 % = practically always dry.

label: Sleepiness rate
tooltip: 0 % = never get sleepy.

label: Stars
tooltip: Vanilla 0.1 - the stars are barely visible. Not play-tested yet.

label: Stash & body ammo bonus
tooltip: Extra rounds handed out to match the weapon caliber, on top of the item list above.

label: Stash & body find chance
tooltip: Chance that a slot yields anything at all. Capped at 100 %, so raising it helps less than the number suggests – many slots already sit close to the cap. Lowering it works in full.

label: Stash clues on bodies
tooltip: Chance that a dead NPC carries a stash clue (vanilla 2 % plus 1 % per clue already found, per region; capped at 100 %). 0 % = never, like 'More Stash Clues' in reverse. Not play-tested yet.

label: Stash & body loot amount
tooltip: How many items a stash or body yields (whole numbers, never below 1).

label: Stash item variety
tooltip: How many different item groups a stash rolls (vanilla 2 to 5, a few up to 15). This is the other axis to the amount slider above: more KINDS of loot rather than bigger piles. Whole numbers, never below one. Not play-tested yet.

label: Sun brightness
tooltip: Vanilla 3.14. Not play-tested yet.

label: Weather duration
tooltip: How long each weather lasts before the next roll using the installed game's durations. Multiplies any regional duration settings. Not play-tested yet.

label: Weather transition speed (experimental)
tooltip: How fast one weather morphs into the next (vanilla multiplier 1 on all 22 transition steps). 200 % = twice as fast. The exact meaning of the multiplier is not verified. Not play-tested yet.

label: Weird artifacts (DLC): charge & duration
tooltip: The Cost of Hope 'weird' artifacts run on a charge (bolt 300) or a timer (flower 2 h). 1000 % = practically no recharge, like 'NoWeirdArtifactRecharge'. Not play-tested yet.

label: Allow mutant looting down to ground level
tooltip: Sets the lower interaction height to zero. The upper height has its own slider. Not play-tested yet.

label: Keep lower-rank NPC equipment in the pool
tooltip: Retains ordinary lower-rank gear within the same faction and equipment slot. Higher ranks can also roll simpler equipment. Not play-tested yet.

label: Extra armor & helmets in ordinary stashes
tooltip: Adds a separate ordinary armor or helmet roll.

label: Extra artifacts in ordinary stashes
tooltip: Adds a separate roll from current ordinary artifact pools; quest and unique artifacts are excluded.

label: Extra attachments in ordinary stashes
tooltip: Adds a separate ordinary weapon attachment roll.

label: Extra weapons in ordinary stashes
tooltip: Adds a separate ordinary weapon roll; quest and unique weapons are excluded.

label: Permanent Weird Flower stealth effect
tooltip: Appends the existing permanent flair-distance effect to Weird Flower. Separate from its charge/duration slider. Not play-tested yet.

label: Moving anomalies / FireBallAnomaly / Pursuit distance (%)
tooltip: Scales this ordinary anomaly variant. Speed changes both base and artifact-influenced maximum speed. Prologue variant, damage and artifact-eating behavior are unchanged. Not play-tested yet.

label: Moving anomalies / FireBallAnomaly / Movement speed including artifact speed-up (%)
tooltip: Scales this ordinary anomaly variant. Speed changes both base and artifact-influenced maximum speed. Prologue variant, damage and artifact-eating behavior are unchanged. Not play-tested yet.

label: Moving anomalies / LightningBallBigAnomaly / Pursuit distance (%)
tooltip: Scales this ordinary anomaly variant. Speed changes both base and artifact-influenced maximum speed. Prologue variant, damage and artifact-eating behavior are unchanged. Not play-tested yet.

label: Moving anomalies / LightningBallBigAnomaly / Movement speed including artifact speed-up (%)
tooltip: Scales this ordinary anomaly variant. Speed changes both base and artifact-influenced maximum speed. Prologue variant, damage and artifact-eating behavior are unchanged. Not play-tested yet.

label: Moving anomalies / LightningBallMediumAnomaly / Pursuit distance (%)
tooltip: Scales this ordinary anomaly variant. Speed changes both base and artifact-influenced maximum speed. Prologue variant, damage and artifact-eating behavior are unchanged. Not play-tested yet.

label: Moving anomalies / LightningBallMediumAnomaly / Movement speed including artifact speed-up (%)
tooltip: Scales this ordinary anomaly variant. Speed changes both base and artifact-influenced maximum speed. Prologue variant, damage and artifact-eating behavior are unchanged. Not play-tested yet.

label: Moving anomalies / LightningBallSmallAnomaly / Pursuit distance (%)
